Amal's Arabic is garbled in places (08:57 'سعود' for صوروا, 10:14 'وحم' for حمس, 43:07 'سيفاء' for عاصفة). Left out as S4 pronunciation: 10:17 'ams' for حمّس (dropped ح), 25:12 inti maz'ooj self-fixed to maz'ooja, 33:44 biniz'aj 'ej sound', 34:54 baz'ajni->biz'ajni self-fix then 'almost', 35:57/36:31 ta'az'aj letter-order slips (she asked 'which goes first, ز or ع'), 49:57-51:28 'matanzajini' for don't annoy me which Amal treated as over-stressed ع (ما تزعجيني), 55:16 شبعان heard as 'hot'. Self-fixes skipped: 44:28 بزعج->بنزعج, 54:52 bansabit->بنبسط, 58:22 أتعبك->أتعبها, 59:18 باتعب->أتعب after لما (B3). 45:27 Amal 'Been catching you saying the [?] instead of the ب' - target word inaudible, no row. 32:06 'shu ra7ty' unclear, Amal 'شو تحكي؟'. 29:25 za'ajatek vs her أزعجتك: she said learn both variants, not filed. Amal ruled at 53:49 that إذا keeps the b- (إذا بكون), which conflicts with buckets.md B3.

Not written (self-fixed before she helped): 'inta baz'aj' -> bitz'aj [33:05], 'بزعج، بنزعج' [44:28], 'ana bansabit' -> بنبسط [54:52], 'باتعب' -> أتعب after لما [59:18], 'هي انزعج' -> انزعجت [41:17]. Medi's 'shu ra7ty' [32:06] is unclear (she answered شو تحكي؟). Medi's 'khalee' [09:37] was accepted as possible but not wanted. agreed.medi_said: Okay, so isn't it en-enbistee? Did you enjoy? ... Oh, I put enbustee.
agreed.amal_said: انبسطتي. ... Yes, it is double T. You forgot the double T and the في.
agreed.why: He dropped the past-tense -t- before the -i ending (enbustee); she recast انبسطتي and said 'it is double T, you forgot the double T'.

agreed.amal_said: But what is it-- what is missing? It's not "انبسطتي." Something is missing. What is it? ... "في" or be?
agreed.why: انبسط takes في/ب before its object (enjoy your time = انبسطتي في وقتك); he left the preposition out and she prompted until he said 'the fee'.
agreed.english: Did you enjoy your time outside?

agreed.amal_said: You put "انبسط". ... does the تخيل have emotions? Does it get happy?
agreed.why: He used انبسط (get happy) where the subject (camping) makes others happy, so it must be بسّط; she prompted 'does camping have emotions?' and he fixed 'this is without the B... el takheem basat'.

agreed.amal_said: كل حدا or what's everyone? ... الكل.
agreed.why: Asked for 'everyone' he offered nafs (self/same), a different word; she supplied الكل. Sheet row: 'all / everyone | Elkul | الكل' (she then also accepted his كل حدا).

agreed.medi_said: Is it, isn't it lisa ma bansabit?
agreed.amal_said: This is I don't get happy yet. What about don't get happy? It's a command. ... Command, so we keep the... ما تنبسط لسه.
agreed.why: 'Don't get happy yet' is a negative command (ما + you-form تنبسط); he gave a negated present ma bansabit (I don't get happy); she named it a command and he reached ma teenbesit.

agreed.medi_said: Ma teenbesit lisa ma ba'arif kul shey.
agreed.amal_said: Ma, we don't know.
agreed.why: The subject is 'we' but he conjugated for 'I' (ba'arif); she prompted 'we don't know' and he fixed to ma ben a'arif.
agreed.english: Don't get happy yet, we don't know everything

agreed.medi_said: Is that the same? Andesit ishish?
agreed.amal_said: انبسطت؟ ... إي.
agreed.why: 'Enjoy something' needs the preposition (انبسطت بإشي); he attached the object directly, she echoed انبسطت؟ and he added 'be'.

agreed.amal_said: ليلة امبارح.
agreed.why: 'Last night' is an idafa: ليلة first, امبارح second, and the feminine first word grows -t (lelet imbare); he tried owner-first and then lele imbare without the -t; she recast ليلة امبارح and he produced lelet imbare.

agreed.amal_said: Mm-mm. We forgot something. ... في ... حفلتك.
agreed.why: انبسط needs في/ب before the object; he said anbisit haflatik with no preposition, she said 'we forgot something' and he added fi.

agreed.amal_said: Mm-mm. I'm gonna keep making you repeat until you say في on your own. ما تنبسط بحالك. That's في or ب.
agreed.why: Same missing preposition (انبسط في/ب): ma tanbisti halak lacks fi/b before halak; she refused it until he said fi halak and recast ما تنبسط بحالك.

agreed.medi_said: And I don't know how to say too much, right?
agreed.amal_said: You can say كتير. كتير or extra. ... زيادة.
agreed.why: He said he did not know 'too much'; she supplied كتير (sheet: 'a lot / very / much | Kteer | كتير'); his 'extra' guess Ziyada was right.

agreed.amal_said: This your night. One night. ... بليلتك. Yes. ليلتك.
agreed.why: ليلة is feminine so 'your night' is ليلتك (the -t comes back before the ending); he said laylak; she prompted 'your night, one night' and he fixed laylatik.

agreed.amal_said: Do you remember متعب؟ ... is tiring. Same pattern as مزعج.
agreed.why: Didn't-know: asked if he remembered متعب he said no and she supplied the meaning (sheet: 'tiring | Mut3eb | متعب').

agreed.amal_said: الأصوات.
agreed.why: Plural of صوت is أصوات; he said swat with the initial أ missing, she recast الأصوات; may be only pronunciation (dropped hamza) rather than a plural-pattern slip.

agreed.medi_said: You guys annoy him. Why is that my favorite? Az'aj, az'ajtu.
agreed.amal_said: أزعجتُ. You can't say أزعجتُ، wo. ... Yes, there is an h.
agreed.why: 'You (pl) annoyed him' needs the object ending on the verb (أزعجتوه); he stopped at az'ajtu; she said you can't say that and pointed to the h at the end.

agreed.medi_said: don't want to annoy them. Ana ma, ma bitti, az'ajkum.
agreed.amal_said: أزعجهم.
agreed.why: 'Them' is the ending -hum, not -kum (you pl); he said az'ajkum, she recast أزعجهم.
agreed.english: I don't want to annoy them

agreed.amal_said: أزعجوه؟
agreed.why: 'Did the kids annoy him' needs the him-ending -h on أزعجوا; he stretched the -uu with no ه and she recast أزعجوه؟ (he still said أزعجو after).

agreed.amal_said: بيزعج، ... بيزعجني.
agreed.why: Subject is هو (he) but he put the plural ending -u on the verb (بيزعجوني = they annoy me); she recast بيزعجني and he repeated it.

agreed.amal_said: بزعجني.
agreed.why: Same slip a minute later for 'it annoys me': plural -u on a singular subject; she recast بزعجني and he asked 'why do I have the o in there?'.
Levantine you(pl) past ending is -tu (انزعجتو), not the MSA -tum he used; she let it pass while he ran the conjugation.

agreed.medi_said: Well, God. أنا نسيت الكلمة. أنا نسيت الكلمة.
agreed.amal_said: سيفاء. [transcript garble of عاصفة]
agreed.why: Didn't-know: he said he forgot the word for storm and she supplied it (he echoed عاصفة [43:09]); sheet row 1400: storm | 3aasefe | عاصفة.

agreed.medi_said: ما تزع-- ما تزعجي. ما تزع-- ما، ما تن-- Oh yeah, that's right. ما تنزعج. ما تنزعج.
agreed.amal_said: تنزعجي. ... ما تنزعجي. Cuz it's ززز، all of them together. ... ما تنزعجي. خلص.
agreed.why: For 'don't get annoyed' he dropped the ن and produced ما تزعجي (don't annoy); she recast ما تنزعجي at 48:13 and 48:33 until he said it [48:39].

agreed.medi_said: It does have an N. ma-matan, matanzajini.
agreed.amal_said: No. ... By me. ما تنزعجي. ... Yes. ما تنزعجي مني. كمان مرة.
agreed.why: انزعج is intransitive: 'by me' is من + ending (مني), not an object ending -ni on the verb; she said No and gave ما تنزعجي مني, he repeated matanzaji minni.

agreed.amal_said: Gets.
agreed.why: 'I get annoyed' is the N-verb بنزعج; he said bazaj (I annoy); she prompted 'gets' and he fixed anabanzaj.

agreed.amal_said: If.
agreed.why: The sentence was 'if I'm hungry'; he started the clause with لما (when) instead of إذا; she said 'If' and he fixed Iza.

agreed.medi_said: Oh, if. Iza. Iza akoon joan.
agreed.amal_said: بس إذا بكون، مش أكون. ليش؟ ... If is conditional، but it doesn't take out the be. It keeps it.
agreed.why: Her ruling: after إذا the ykoon form keeps its b- (إذا بكون), he dropped it (akoon); he fixed iza bakoon. Note this contradicts buckets.md B3 which lists iza among b-drop words - Amal's rule wins.
agreed.english: I get annoyed if I'm hungry

agreed.amal_said: mean or what's the better one؟ The one who. يلي.
agreed.why: 'I annoy who(ever) annoys me' needs the relative اللي/يلي, not the question word مين; she prompted 'the one who' and he said اللي.

agreed.medi_said: اللي who annoys me. Okay. So، اه، بينزعجني.
agreed.amal_said: ليش أن annoys me. ... ✓ mm-hmm.
agreed.why: 'annoys me' is the make-verb بيزعجني; he used the get-verb with an object (بينزعجني); she asked 'ليش أن? annoys me' and he fixed بيزعجني.

agreed.amal_said: I didn't get.
agreed.why: 'I wasn't annoyed' needs ما before the verb; he said the affirmative أنا انزعجت; she prompted 'I didn't get' and he fixed أنا ما انزعجت.

agreed.medi_said: اه، أنا، اه، زعلان. ... زعلان، زعلان.
agreed.amal_said: زعلت. ... Here's your inter-internal flip. زعلت. ... أنا ما انزعجت، أنا زعلت.
agreed.why: For 'I was sad' (past, parallel to ما انزعجت) he used the present-state adjective زعلان with no past marker; she recast the past verb زعلت three times. Sheet rows 1164 (Za3laan) and 675 (Ana baz3al).
Signing off he said تعال (come here) where a goodbye (يلا / سلام / بشوفك) fits; may be a transcription slip; Amal only said Bye. Best reading marked as B.

r2.medi_said: so I, I think I remembered mazuj as annoying and moza- mozaj as annoyed.

r2.right: ليش مختلف عن / ليش فيه فرق

r2.why: Object -ك (you) for 'her' after she had prompted 'Her.'; he corrected to أتعبها in the same turn and she confirmed.

r2.why: Plural command of صوّر; she cut in twice with a recast right after 'saweroo' (transcribed as سعود) and he re-said 'Sawroo'; her line is garbled in the transcript so the exact fix is uncertain.

r2.medi_said: el takheem basat kul hadha oo ams.

r2.medi_said: So, inti, are you annoyed? Inti maz'ooj min ishi?
r2.amal_said: إنت مزعوج من إشي؟ ... Oh, إنتي مزعوجة. Yes. إنتي مزعوجة من إشي؟
r2.why: Feminine subject inti with masculine adjective maz'ooj; she echoed the masculine form, he caught it (maz'ooja [25:27]) and she confirmed إنتي مزعوجة; mostly his own fix after her echo.

r2.amal_said: أزعجتك. ... See? It's easier to say أزعجتك.
r2.why: She had asked for the a- form (أزعج) and recast his za'ajatek as أزعجتك; he accepted 'Oh, that's right, az'ajet'. Both forms are valid per her [28:13], so this is drill-specific.

r2.medi_said: So, hadha al-jaw, annoys me. Baz- baz'ajni. Ana biyaz...
r2.why: First-person prefix ba- on a verb whose subject is 'this weather' (3rd m.); she said 'almost' and modelled بيزعجني, he repeated biz'ajni.

r2.medi_said: So, don't annoy me. Ma ta'az-- Ma ta-- Ma ta'az'ajni. Ma ta'az'aj.
r2.amal_said: Which goes first؟ الـ ز أو الـ ع؟ ... ممتاز. ما تزعجني.
r2.why: He built the negative command from the a- past form (ma ta-az'aj) with an extra vowel/glottal before ز; she prompted 'which goes first, ز or ع?' until he said 'ma tiz'ajni' [36:22].

r2.amal_said: ما تزعجيني. ... تزعجيني. ... ✓ Yes. ما تزعجيني.
r2.why: Same extra a- in the feminine negative command; she recast ما تزعجيني twice [36:35, 36:44] until he said it right [36:48].

r2.medi_said: هو منزعج بي... نز-نزعج؟ Or is it انزعج؟
r2.amal_said: Just like we did in إنزع. Yes. Just like we did with انبسط.
r2.why: Asked for the past of بنزعج he offered the participle منزعج then 'نزعج' before guessing انزعج; she confirmed by analogy with انبسط.

r2.amal_said: بننزعج. ... Been catching you saying the instead of the ب.
r2.why: She said she has been catching him saying another letter (likely م-) instead of the ب on the we-form; the transcript normalises his form so the slip itself is not visible.

r2.medi_said: Oh, oh, oh, okay. تستعمل الـ-- يتستعمل الـ telephone.
r2.why: Echoing her بستعمل as a statement to her, he dropped the b- and the feminine -i (تستعمل); she let it pass. 'telephone' is her own word here and is not on the sheet, so not tier 3.
